A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CypherBench and contain 28 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A and B. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the scientific content and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 LLMs on CypherBench in Table 3, performance breakdowns in Figure 5, and manually annotated error analysis in Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original LLM evaluations, performance breakdowns, and error analysis in Section 6, Table 3, and Figures 5–6.

M1.justification: The RDF-to-property-graph transformation, template-based task generation, question rewriting and verification, and text-to-Cypher procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 11 domain graphs and graph-pattern tasks. Evaluation still covers the same seven test domains; the added literature does not introduce evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 evaluates the same 12 LLMs in both versions. PoG, KARPA, WikiSP, and SPINACH are added to the literature overview in Table 5, without being evaluated as new comparators.

E3.justification: The reported protocol is identical: the 8,817/2,488 train/test split, zero-shot prompting, EX/PSJS/executability metrics, and 120-second query timeout are retained, as are the appendix prompts.

E4.justification: Sections 6.3–6.6 retain the same pattern, template, and domain breakdowns and error analysis of 50 incorrect predictions per selected model. Appendix A.5 and Table 13 retain the same error taxonomy and examples.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the LLM evaluations.

E6.justification: All experimental scores, plots, and appendix statistics are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports the same execution accuracies of 61.58% for claude3.5-sonnet and 60.18% for gpt-4o in both versions.

T1.justification: The graph and task definitions, graph-pattern constructions, and EX and PSJS definitions in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. No mathematical derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about property-graph views, the transformation engine, CypherBench, task generation, and evaluation metrics.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model performance and error mechanisms in Section 6 are unchanged. Section 4.5 still preserves entity names during rewriting and leaves entity linking for future work; the appendix's schema-fetching caveats also remain.

D1.justification: Deployment details, API information, execution settings, dataset/code links, and Appendix A's prompts and schema-fetching procedures are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same graph statistics and schemas.

R1.justification: Section 7.1 and Table 5 add PoG, KARPA, WikiSP, and SPINACH, with four new references. v1's concluding contrast with earlier systems is replaced by explicit acknowledgment that SPINACH operates over full Wikidata using an agentic workflow.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to Section 7.1, Table 5 terminology, references, and the added EURECOM author affiliation. The section organization and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 5 updates its retrieval-category label and method entries within the existing structure. The affiliation line changes and references reflow across pages 19–20. All figures and appendix tables retain identical renderings.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves research positioning by covering four additional works and acknowledging SPINACH's full-Wikidata workflow in Section 7.1, replacing v1's broader contrast with prior systems. This makes the literature comparison more complete and qualified. Methods, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
